2014_subclasses.kensei.description: Monks of the Way of the Kensei train relentlessly with their weapons, to the point where they become extensions of their body. Founded on a mastery of sword fighting, the tradition has expanded to include many different weapons.
2014_subclasses.kensei.path-of-the-kense: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies. You also choose two types of Kensei Weapons: melee weapons or ranged weapons. You can change your choices each time you gain a level. You can use your choice of any Kensei Weapon as a monk weapon, and when you do so, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your Kensei Weapons.
Choose two types of melee weapons to be your kensei weapons. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls with these weapons.
Choose one ranged weapon to be your kensei weapon. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls with this weapon.
Gain proficiency with martial weapons and calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies. (action).
2014_subclasses.kensei.one-with-the-blad: At 6th level, you extend your ki into your kensei weapons. When you hit a creature with a kensei weapon, you can spend 1 ki point to do one of the following: add your Wisdom modifier to the damage of the attack, or the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you.
Can spend 1 ki point to do one of the following: add your Wisdom modifier to the damage of the attack, or the target must succeed on a Strength saving.
2014_subclasses.kensei.sharpen-the-blade: At 11th level, you gain the ability to augment your weapons with your ki. As a bonus action, you can spend up to 3 ki points to grant a kensei weapon you touch a bonus to attack and damage rolls when you attack with it. The bonus equals the number of ki points you spent. The bonus lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature again. This feature has no effect on a magic weapon that already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls.
Has no effect on a magic weapon that already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.kensei.unerring-accuracy: Starting at 17th level, your mastery of the blade ensures that your strikes land. If you miss with an attack roll using a monk weapon on your turn, you can reroll the attack roll, and you must use the new roll. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.
Can reroll the attack roll, and you must use the new roll. (action).
